claims: Erectile dysfunction (ED) is commonly known as impotence.
Erectile dysfunction is the persistent inability to achieve or maintain a firm erection for sexual intercourse.
ED affects roughly half of men between 40-70.
ED is often caused by physical issues like diabetes.
ED is often caused by physical issues like heart disease.
ED is often caused by physical issues like reduced blood flow.
ED can stem from psychological factors such as stress.
ED can stem from psychological factors such as anxiety.
Physical symptoms of ED include reduced firmness or frequency of morning erections.
Physical symptoms of ED include inability to maintain an erection.
Physical symptoms of ED include reduced sexual desire (libido).
Causes of ED include high-fat diets.
Causes of ED include excessive alcohol consumption.
Causes of ED include chronic health conditions like diabetes.
Causes of ED include hypertension.
Causes of ED include low testosterone.
Common interventions for ED include oral medications (Viagra, Cialis, Levitra, Stendra).
Common interventions for ED include vacuum erection devices (penis pumps).
Common interventions for ED include testosterone therapy.
Common interventions for ED include psychological counseling.
Impotence is the most direct medical synonym for erectile dysfunction.
Erection problems are commonly used to describe ED.
Sexual dysfunction is a broader term covering ED.
Psychogenic ED is specific to ED caused by stress, anxiety, or depression.
ED affects 5-10% of men under 40.
Up to 80% of men in their 80s report some degree of ED.
Common treatments for ED include lifestyle changes such as quitting smoking.
Common treatments for ED include medication.
